approach: Sum the gravitational potential energy of every pair of particles: two pairs sit on the 3l₀ sides, two on the 4l₀ sides, and two on the 5l₀ diagonals.

steps.text: Set the rectangle's sides as 3l₀ and 4l₀, so each diagonal is the hypotenuse of a 3-4-5 triangle.
List every distinct pair among the four particles. The four sides give two pairs of length 3l₀ and two pairs of length 4l₀, and the two diagonals both have length 5l₀.
Write the gravitational potential energy of one pair as −Gm²/r and add it once for each of the six pairs.
steps.why_this_step: Each of the six pairs contributes exactly once; there is no double counting to correct for.

steps.text: Add the reciprocal separations over a common denominator of 30.
Write the size of the potential energy in the required units.

common_mistakes.text: Adding only the four sides and leaving out the two diagonal pairs gives 2/3 + 1/2 = 7/6.
Finding the correct sum over all six pairs, then halving it on the mistaken idea that each pair's energy is being counted twice, gives 47/60.
Using only one 3l₀ side and one 4l₀ side, missing the matching sides and both diagonals entirely, gives 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12.
